Return JSON with guidance (max6000 characters), change_reason, and direct_solution (boolean; true if supplying instance-specific repair values). Keep evidence checks, uncertainty, applicability and one-variable experiments. No safety, speed or evaluator changes. Existing guidance:# Robot problem solving protocol v2

Use scripts/agent_loop.py --arm D in the existing MuJoCo Python environment for complete recorded offline collection. scripts/learn.py remains the low-level simulation adapter; headless success is not a complete Episode. Keep existing robot APIs and safety limits.

1. Specify physical completion independently of API acceptance. Record task, version, initial state, action, expected and observed physical effects, earliest anomaly and final outcome. Missing observations remain UNKNOWN.
2. Retrieve at most five memory records matching task, failure signature and applicability. Read evidence references, not whole videos or chat histories.
3. Separate observations from hypotheses. Propose at most three causes, each with a falsifiable, low-cost experiment. A model explanation alone is not verification. Distinguish the first observed anomaly from the true onset if sampling is incomplete.
4. Compare the proposed repair and action fingerprint with negative experiences. Do not repeat an ineffective repair under the same conditions without new evidence. A repair after the earliest anomaly requires an explicit causal explanation.
5. Change one variable in the existing MuJoCo interface. Save config/source hashes, inputs, full local evidence references, metrics, failures and exceptions. Do not tune friction or delete collisions just to pass.
6. Replay original condition and predeclared held-out initial states. Promote only within the validated scope; record regressions and restore the previous active version on failure.
7. REAL_VERIFIED requires physical success evidence, simulation validation, existing safety checks and fresh human permission. SIMULATION_VERIFIED never authorizes hardware.
8. Persist JSON + Markdown for every attempt, including timeout and infrastructure failures. Run publish.py with explicit paths after each completed round; keep local commits on push failure.

## UNKNOWN TASK MODE / Exploration Protocol

State the goal and observable completion; split into subgoals; retrieve available skills with applicability; explicitly list unknown transitions. Generate <=3 candidate plans and predict each observable outcome. Prefer reversible simulator probes that separate hypotheses under equal budgets. Observe, update or reject hypotheses, and stop repeating contradicted plans. If evidence is insufficient, retain UNKNOWN and select the next discriminating observation. Promote a reusable skill only after independent initial-state validation. Never substitute a memorized unseen-task answer for this process.

## Metrics

Report task success, unseen-task success, repeated-failure rate, new skills, tokens, inference wall time, simulated time, actual robot time and interventions separately. Missing measurements are null, not zero. Deterministic software-policy tests are not weak-LLM capability evaluations. Calibration requires bounded parameters, real measured targets and held-out real data; otherwise defer it.

## Simulation privileged information

Simulator object/goal poses, contact state, velocities and task ground truth may be used in every simulation stage. Each result must disclose the fields actually used and mark conclusions Simulation-only. Model comparisons must expose the same information to each group, or explicitly separate observation access from method effects. Privileged access does not authorize changing success detectors, physical parameters or hardware safety rules. Count a successful collection Episode only after its existing-format videos, state/action arrays and physics replay are verified; headless success alone is insufficient.

## Executable memory and current scope

Record actual_planner_kind and model_invoked. Retention loss observed during transport takes precedence over a later IK exception when selecting what to investigate; do not infer friction or measured force. The native success and safety detectors stay independent. All full collection passes the existing Episode verifier, including failures. Current evidence does not establish unknown-task-family competence, real calibration or total-cost reduction.

## Spatial disagreement observed on 2026-11-16

Use bounded, simulation-validated noncontact observation commands under the existing hardware conditions; a successful observation sequence is not a successful task Episode. Report command-array equality separately from actual execution timing.

A scene-only calibration fit must also be checked against robot-attached geometry and withheld views. Reprojection improvement or a fitted22mm translation alone is not a measured object correction. Reject unsupported transforms without a hardware retry; retain the old configuration and record the next missing measurement. Evidence and scope: experiments/spatial_cycle6/REPORT.md and NE014. # Robot problem solving protocol v3 — evidence-gated tool use

Preserve existing safety, speed, recording, success and evaluator criteria. In a bounded harness, use only supplied allowlisted functions and schemas; repository script names are not permission to invoke shell, files, network or hardware. Return one schema-valid tool request or final plan per step. Never claim execution from a proposal.

1. Establish the evidence scope. Separate archived episode observations, requested configuration, resolved execution configuration, newly executed trajectories and real measurements. Record source/configuration hashes, active arm, target, startup, units and observation provenance. Configuration resolution is not trajectory verification. Changed state invalidates unverified reuse of old joint references and final residuals; do not assume an offset response. Unknown changed values remain UNKNOWN.

2. Specify observable physical completion independently of API acceptance. Keep facts, hypotheses and UNKNOWN separate. Record expected versus observed effects, earliest observed anomaly and final outcome. Sampled observations do not identify exact physical onset. Do not invent a failure in a successful baseline or infer stable grasp from absence of detected retention loss. Release, retreat and sustained seating evidence remain subject to existing success criteria.

3. Use tools to answer a specific unresolved question. Before a call, identify the missing evidence, the decision it could change and its budget cost. Reuse supplied summaries rather than querying identical evidence without a reason. Retrieve at most five applicable memory records with evidence references. Match simulator/source, embodiment, target, initial state, units and observation access. Historical warnings and different-profile results are analogies, not current-scene facts or replayable motions.

4. Check permitted experiment dimensions and bounds before selecting a change. An empty allowed-value list supplies no candidate for that parameter; an empty rejected-value list does not authorize arbitrary values. Do not infer that all experiments are impossible from one unavailable parameter. Consider another dimension or observation only if explicitly supported by the available interface, evidence and remaining budget. Never invent tool capabilities, bounds or repair values.

5. Generate at most three falsifiable simulation hypotheses. For each, state the supporting observation, remaining uncertainty, one permitted independent variable, fixed controls, predicted observable result and rejection condition. An UNKNOWN real cause does not by itself prohibit a bounded simulation hypothesis test using privileged evidence. Such a test establishes only simulation behavior, not a real repair or calibration. A successful archived baseline may support a justified sensitivity or applicability test; it does not require an arbitrary repair.

6. Select the lowest-cost discriminating experiment under the actual budget. Change one variable, preserving speed, safety, physical parameters, recording requirements and native evaluators. Do not alter friction, remove collisions or change success detectors to pass. Compare action fingerprints with negative experiences; repeat ineffective changes only with new applicable evidence. If an anomaly is observed, prioritize it over later exceptions and explain any proposed downstream intervention causally.

7. Treat simulator poses, velocities, contacts and task ground truth as privileged Simulation-only evidence; disclose the fields actually used. Contact pairs do not establish active constraint, gripping force or measured force. Motor opening is not six-axis force. No observed retention loss does not exclude sliding or rotation. This robot's real visual evidence is RGB only; unverified depth files are not real measurements. Keep model-comparison observation access equal or separately report access effects.

8. Stop precisely when no supported experiment remains. State the unavailable permission, bound, observation or budget item; distinguish unsupported hypothesis, exhausted budget, unavailable action and model/schema error. List unresolved questions and the next evidence needed. Do not report budget exhaustion without budget evidence, or treat a MODEL_ERROR status as proof that no experiment exists. Missing execution feedback means no newly verified execution result.

9. Validate before promotion. Compare the original condition and predeclared independent initial states without tuning to held-out results. Promote only within the tested applicability scope; preserve the previous active version and restore it on regression. Record actual planner kind and model invocation. Compiled policies require their existing applicability checks. Simulation verification never establishes unknown-task-family competence, real calibration or total-cost reduction.

10. Preserve complete evidence accounting. Save hashes, inputs, references, metrics, exceptions and failures through authorized interfaces. Complete Episodes require the existing videos, state/action arrays, schema/units checks and physics replay verification; headless trials and configuration resolution are not Episodes. Keep intermediate artifacts outside formal dataset roots. Persist JSON and Markdown and publish only through authorized workflow interfaces. Missing measurements are null, not zero; report task outcomes, tokens, inference time, simulated time, robot time and interventions separately.

11. Keep real-transfer gates unchanged. Real movement requires fresh explicit permission, validated simulation and existing safety checks. Spatial disagreement requires checking camera, attached geometry, scene placement and matching coordinates before unsupported grasp or contact changes. Software FK consistency and reprojection improvement alone are not physical calibration. Calibration requires bounded parameters, measured real targets and held-out real validation. Retain UNKNOWN causes and old configurations when evidence is insufficient; no simulation probe authorizes hardware.
